result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You were in hospital from 5 October 2026 to 7 October 2026. You had a chest infection (community-acquired pneumonia). It was in the lower part of your right lung (right lower lobe).

Your CURB-65 score is 1. Doctors use this score to judge how serious a chest infection is.

You may feel tired for several weeks. Your cough may last 3 to 6 weeks.

## What you need to do
1. Take your amoxicillin tablets for 3 more days. Your last dose is on 10 October 2026.
2. Go to your repeat chest X-ray (CXR) in 6 weeks. It is at the Radiology Department. It checks that the infection has cleared.
3. Do not book the chest X-ray. A request has already been sent.

## Dates and medicines
- 5 October 2026: you went into hospital.
- 7 October 2026: you left hospital.
- 10 October 2026: your last dose of amoxicillin.
- In 6 weeks: repeat chest X-ray at the Radiology Department. There is no exact date yet.

Medicine: Amoxicillin (antibiotic)
- Dose: 500 milligrams.
- How often: 3 times a day (TDS).
- Change: continue.
- You had 1 day of antibiotics through a drip (IV) in hospital. Now you take tablets. You take them for 3 more days. That makes 5 days of antibiotics in total. 2 days were already given in hospital.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- How will I know the infection has cleared?
- When will I get the date for my chest X-ray?
- How long will the tiredness and cough last for me?

## When to get urgent help
See your GP or call 111 if:
- you become more short of breath.
- your fever comes back.
- you cough up blood.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
